title: Audio Evaluation — WER, CER, MOS, FAD, EER, and MMAU

questions.question: What does wer("a b c", "a x c") return?
questions.explanation: After normalization there is one substitution in a three-word reference, so edit distance divided by reference length is 1/3.

questions.question: Which preprocessing does cer perform before computing its character edit distance?
options: It lowercases text and removes punctuation
It performs no normalization; it compares list(ref) with list(hyp) directly
It splits on whitespace and discards repeated words
It converts both strings into MFCC vectors
questions.explanation: Unlike wer, cer calls _edit_distance(list(ref), list(hyp)) without calling normalize.

questions.question: At threshold t, which pair of conditions does eer_from_scores use?
options: Both rates count scores strictly above t from the same list
FAR counts same scores >= t, and FRR counts diff scores < t
FAR counts diff scores >= t, and FRR counts same scores < t
FAR counts diff scores < t, and FRR counts same scores >= t
questions.explanation: The function treats a high similarity as an accept: fake/diff scores at least t are false accepts, while genuine/same scores below t are false rejects.

questions.question: Which terms make up embedding_fad_like's distance?
options: Only the difference between the two embedding means
The fraction of correct multiple-choice answers
The squared mean-distance term plus squared distance between square-root variances
questions.explanation: The function sums squared mean differences and squared differences of standard deviations, then takes the square root.

questions.question: If mmau_accuracy receives 3 matching predictions out of 4, what value does it return?
questions.explanation: It counts equal prediction/gold pairs and divides by four, giving 3/4=0.75.

questions.question: Which metric pairing best matches the tasks in this lesson?
options: WER for watermark payload recovery, EER for word order, and FAD for turn timing
WER/CER for transcription, EER for speaker verification, and FAD-like distance for embedding distributions
CER for codebook bitrate, MMAU for microphone gain, and EER for punctuation style
FAD for exact transcript edits, WER for speaker identity, and MMAU for sample rate
questions.explanation: The demo implements edit rates for text, equal-error analysis for speaker scores, and a mean/variance distance for generated embedding distributions.
